applicationInfo.name: Threat Model Export
applicationInfo.description: IRIS is a cloud-native AI-powered code analysis and chat application built on AWS. It allows users to upload codebases to S3, generates summaries and context using Amazon Bedrock LLMs (Claude models), and provides a real-time WebSocket-based chat interface for querying code. The system uses a React frontend served via CloudFront, a FastAPI WebSocket backend on ECS Fargate, Cognito for authentication, S3 for codebase storage, and DynamoDB for optional conversation logging. It also exposes an MCP server for IDE integration.

assumptions.content: Cognito is properly configured in production deployments with self-signup disabled
VPC endpoints are configured for all AWS service access (S3, Bedrock, CloudWatch, ECR)
Amazon Bedrock does not retain or use customer prompts for model training
No role-based access control (RBAC) exists - all authenticated users have equal access to all features and codebases

mitigations.content: Enforce Cognito configuration as mandatory in production deployments. Add startup validation that fails fast if USER_POOL_ID and USER_POOL_CLIENT_ID are not set. Remove the anonymous fallback behavior.

Implement prompt injection detection and prevention. Add input sanitization for user queries before sending to Bedrock. Use system prompt hardening techniques and output validation to prevent LLM manipulation.

Implement role-based access control (RBAC) to restrict user access to specific codebases. Add resource-level authorization checks that validate user permissions before granting access to codebase data.
Implement WebSocket connection rate limiting and per-user session limits. Add Bedrock API call budgets and throttling to prevent cost escalation from abuse.

Tighten Content Security Policy by removing unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval directives. Use nonce-based CSP for inline scripts. Implement output encoding for all AI-generated content rendered in the frontend.
Enable Customer Managed Keys (CMK) for DynamoDB encryption when conversation logging is enabled. Implement data retention policies and automatic purging of old conversation data.

Implement S3 bucket policy best practices: block public access, enforce encryption, restrict access to specific IAM roles, enable versioning and access logging. Use VPC endpoint policies to restrict S3 access.
Implement dependency scanning in CI/CD pipeline. Pin dependency versions. Use private package registry. Regularly audit and update dependencies for known vulnerabilities.

Implement short-lived JWT tokens with automatic refresh. Add token binding to prevent replay attacks. Consider implementing WebSocket-level session tokens that are distinct from authentication tokens.
Apply least-privilege IAM policies for ECS task roles. Separate read and write permissions. Use condition keys to restrict access to specific resources. Enable IMDSv2 to protect container metadata.

threats.prerequisites: when Cognito environment variables (USER_POOL_ID, USER_POOL_CLIENT_ID) are not configured
threats.threatAction: access the system without authentication since the backend falls back to anonymous mode, granting default claims (sub: anonymous)
threats.threatImpact: complete unauthenticated access to all system features in local/Docker environments only — CDK cloud deployments always provision Cognito
threats.statement: An unauthenticated attacker, when running locally or via Docker without Cognito environment variables configured, can access the system without authentication since the backend falls back to anonymous mode. In cloud (CDK) deployments, Cognito is always provisioned and injected into the ECS task, so this threat does not apply to production.

threats.prerequisites: with authenticated access to the WebSocket chat interface
threats.threatAction: craft malicious prompts to manipulate the LLM agent into revealing system prompts, accessing unauthorized files via the file retrieval agent, or executing unintended tool calls through the agentic framework
threats.threatImpact: unauthorized access to customer source code, exfiltration of system prompts, or unintended information disclosure via agent tool calls
threats.statement: A An authenticated user with authenticated access to the WebSocket chat interface can craft malicious prompts to manipulate the LLM agent into revealing system prompts, accessing unauthorized files via the file retrieval agent, or executing unintended tool calls through the agentic framework, which leads to unauthorized access to customer source code, exfiltration of system prompts, or unintended information disclosure via agent tool calls

threats.prerequisites: with access to the AWS account or misconfigured S3 bucket policies
threats.threatAction: access the S3 codebase artifacts bucket directly, bypassing application-level controls, due to overly permissive bucket policies or IAM permissions
threats.threatImpact: direct access to all customer source code stored in the S3 bucket, bypassing all application security controls
threats.statement: A An insider or external attacker with access to the AWS account or misconfigured S3 bucket policies can access the S3 codebase artifacts bucket directly, bypassing application-level controls, due to overly permissive bucket policies or IAM permissions, which leads to direct access to all customer source code stored in the S3 bucket, bypassing all application security controls

threats.threatSource: An attacker with access to AWS internal network
threats.prerequisites: with ability to intercept traffic between CloudFront and ALB
threats.threatAction: intercept unencrypted HTTP traffic between CloudFront and ALB (which uses HTTP over AWS internal network) to capture JWT tokens, user queries, or code analysis results
threats.threatImpact: exposure of authentication tokens, user queries containing sensitive code context, and AI-generated responses
threats.statement: A An attacker with access to AWS internal network with ability to intercept traffic between CloudFront and ALB can intercept unencrypted HTTP traffic between CloudFront and ALB (which uses HTTP over AWS internal network) to capture JWT tokens, user queries, or code analysis results, which leads to exposure of authentication tokens, user queries containing sensitive code context, and AI-generated responses

threats.prerequisites: with ability to exploit unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval CSP directives in the frontend
threats.threatAction: inject malicious JavaScript via the chat interface that executes in other users' browsers, leveraging the CSP's unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval directives
threats.threatImpact: theft of JWT tokens, session hijacking, or manipulation of the chat interface to display misleading AI responses
threats.statement: A An attacker with ability to exploit unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval CSP directives in the frontend can inject malicious JavaScript via the chat interface that executes in other users' browsers, leveraging the CSP's unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval directives, which leads to theft of JWT tokens, session hijacking, or manipulation of the chat interface to display misleading AI responses

threats.prerequisites: with access to a stolen or leaked JWT token
threats.threatAction: replay the JWT token to establish a WebSocket connection and impersonate the legitimate user's session
threats.threatImpact: full access to the impersonated user's session, including their codebase analysis results and conversation history
threats.statement: A An external attacker with access to a stolen or leaked JWT token can replay the JWT token to establish a WebSocket connection and impersonate the legitimate user's session, which leads to full access to the impersonated user's session, including their codebase analysis results and conversation history

threats.prerequisites: with code execution inside the ECS container (e.g., via container escape or supply chain attack)
threats.threatAction: access the ECS task role credentials from the container metadata service to gain direct access to Bedrock, S3, DynamoDB, and KMS
threats.threatImpact: full access to all AWS services the task role can access, including customer source code in S3 and Bedrock model invocation
threats.statement: A An attacker with code execution inside the ECS container (e.g., via container escape or supply chain attack) can access the ECS task role credentials from the container metadata service to gain direct access to Bedrock, S3, DynamoDB, and KMS, which leads to full access to all AWS services the task role can access, including customer source code in S3 and Bedrock model invocation

threats.prerequisites: with authenticated access to the system
threats.threatAction: inject crafted input to create misleading log entries or deny performing actions when audit trails are insufficient
threats.threatImpact: inability to attribute malicious actions to specific users, corrupted audit trails, or false log entries that mislead incident response
threats.statement: A A malicious user with authenticated access to the system can inject crafted input to create misleading log entries or deny performing actions when audit trails are insufficient, which leads to inability to attribute malicious actions to specific users, corrupted audit trails, or false log entries that mislead incident response

threats.threatSource: A malicious IDE plugin or compromised MCP client
threats.prerequisites: with access to the local developer machine running the MCP server
threats.threatAction: exploit the MCP server's codebase_context or codebase_query tools to access files outside the intended codebase directory via path traversal
threats.threatImpact: access to sensitive files on the developer's machine beyond the intended codebase scope
threats.statement: A A malicious IDE plugin or compromised MCP client with access to the local developer machine running the MCP server can exploit the MCP server's codebase_context or codebase_query tools to access files outside the intended codebase directory via path traversal, which leads to access to sensitive files on the developer's machine beyond the intended codebase scope

threats.prerequisites: with network access to the CloudFront endpoint
threats.threatAction: open many concurrent WebSocket connections to exhaust ECS Fargate container memory (in-memory session store) or trigger excessive Bedrock API calls, causing resource exhaustion or cost escalation
threats.threatImpact: service unavailability for legitimate users, excessive AWS costs from Bedrock API abuse, or container OOM crashes
threats.statement: A An external attacker with network access to the CloudFront endpoint can open many concurrent WebSocket connections to exhaust ECS Fargate container memory (in-memory session store) or trigger excessive Bedrock API calls, causing resource exhaustion or cost escalation, which leads to service unavailability for legitimate users, excessive AWS costs from Bedrock API abuse, or container OOM crashes

threats.threatAction: access codebases and conversation histories belonging to other users since no role-based access control or resource-level authorization exists
threats.threatImpact: unauthorized access to other users' proprietary source code and conversation data, violating data isolation in multi-tenant deployments
threats.statement: A A malicious authenticated user with valid authentication credentials can access codebases and conversation histories belonging to other users since no role-based access control or resource-level authorization exists, which leads to unauthorized access to other users' proprietary source code and conversation data, violating data isolation in multi-tenant deployments

threats.threatSource: An insider with DynamoDB read access
threats.prerequisites: when DynamoDB conversation logging is enabled without CMK encryption
threats.threatAction: access conversation history stored in DynamoDB which may contain sensitive code snippets, proprietary logic, or security-relevant information discussed in chat
threats.threatImpact: exposure of sensitive conversation data including code snippets, architectural details, and security discussions
threats.statement: A An insider with DynamoDB read access when DynamoDB conversation logging is enabled without CMK encryption can access conversation history stored in DynamoDB which may contain sensitive code snippets, proprietary logic, or security-relevant information discussed in chat, which leads to exposure of sensitive conversation data including code snippets, architectural details, and security discussions

threats.prerequisites: when third-party Python packages are installed in the Docker image
threats.threatAction: compromise a third-party dependency (e.g., via typosquatting or package takeover) to inject malicious code into the container, gaining access to customer data and AWS credentials
threats.threatImpact: full compromise of the application container, access to customer source code, IAM credentials, and ability to exfiltrate data
threats.statement: A A supply chain attacker when third-party Python packages are installed in the Docker image can compromise a third-party dependency (e.g., via typosquatting or package takeover) to inject malicious code into the container, gaining access to customer data and AWS credentials, which leads to full compromise of the application container, access to customer source code, IAM credentials, and ability to exfiltrate data
